statement: Whenever number_of_permutations n requirements returns a result r, r = (N mod 1000000007), where N is the number of sequences perm of length n such that: (1) perm is a permutation of {0,1,...,n-1}, i.e. every perm[k] is in 0..n-1 and all entries are distinct; and (2) for every i with 0 <= i < len(requirements), inv(perm, requirements[i][0]) = requirements[i][1]. Here, for a sequence perm and an integer e with 0 <= e < n, inv(perm,e) is the number of pairs (a,b) such that 0 <= a < b <= e and perm[a] > perm[b].
preconditions: Let m = len(requirements). The input satisfies all problem constraints: 2 <= n <= 300; 1 <= m <= n; each requirements[i] has length exactly 2; for every i with 0 <= i < m, writing e_i = requirements[i][0] and c_i = requirements[i][1], we have 0 <= e_i <= n - 1 and 0 <= c_i <= 400; the e_i are pairwise distinct; and there is an index i with e_i = n - 1.
